title: ACA s. 31 — Form and contents of arbitral award

content.overview: Section 31 prescribes the formal and substantive requirements of an arbitral award, including writing and signature, reasons subject to statutory exceptions, date and place, delivery of a signed copy, and statutory rules concerning interest and costs.
content.glance: Section 31 prescribes the formal and substantive requirements of an arbitral award, including writing and signature, reasons subject to statutory exceptions, date and place, delivery of a signed copy, and statutory rules concerning interest and costs.
content.study:
Module 1: Writing and signatures
The award must be in writing and signed by the members of the arbitral tribunal in accordance with section 31. Where there is more than one arbitrator, the statutory majority/signature rule applies, with the dissenting-signature proviso operating as prescribed.

Module 2: Reasons
The award must state reasons unless the parties have agreed that no reasons are to be given or the award is an award on agreed terms under section 30.

Module 3: Date, place and delivery
The award states its date and the place of arbitration, and a signed copy is delivered to each party.

Module 4: Interest
Section 31 contains the statutory framework for pre-award and post-award interest, subject to party agreement and the express terms of the provision.

Module 5: Costs
Section 31's costs provision must now be read with section 31A; the award may determine costs subject to the Act's statutory costs regime.

provisions.title: Form and contents of arbitral award

examples.title: Rule applies
examples.body: A final award is written, signed, reasoned, dated and states the place of arbitration, and a signed copy is delivered to each party.

examples.title: Rule fails or changes
examples.body: An award gives no reasons even though no statutory exception applies; the tribunal must satisfy the section 31 requirement to state reasons.

hypotheticals.question: Are reasons always mandatory?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 31 recognises specified exceptions, including party agreement that no reasons are required and an award on agreed terms under section 30.

distinctions.title: Reasons and formal requirements
distinctions.right: Reasoned written award subject to statutory exceptions
distinctions.rows: Award on agreed terms/other statutory exception may alter the reasons requirement.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 31 as merely a formatting provision.
misconceptions.correction: It regulates core award validity requirements as well as interest and costs consequences; each subsection must be tested separately.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 31 regulate?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: It prescribes the form and contents of an arbitral award and includes rules on reasons, date/place, delivery, interest and costs.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: Map the award against each applicable subsection before advising on challenge or enforcement.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should section 31 be applied in submissions?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Start with the statutory text, identify every condition and then apply the facts to the precise statutory consequence.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: Keep the submission statute-led and distinguish discretion, conditions and consequence.
